# hazard render — source mismatches (renderer notes; rendered as the source states them, never rendered around)

Source: tasks/road_hazard_claims/hazard.extended.yaml (sha256 4abb11fb...), task_tools.py (sha256 4ede7327...).

## Assembly sentences naming several factor quantities (no factor-silent home possible)
1. hazard_ext_lot_cancellation_refund (compute_basis.result): "Any Life-of-Tread unused-call credit is added to, and any Life-of-Tread bundle clawback is taken from, the Life-of-Tread cancellation refund before that refund is rounded and held at 0.00 or more." — names two factor quantities (call credit, bundle clawback); not in baseline.rule.
2. hazard_ext_counter_replacement_posting (compute_basis.counter_pct): "Counter-replacement points from the four schedules below are added only to a prorated counter-replacement coverage percentage, the sum then being held between 0 and 100; a counter-replacement coverage percentage of 100 under the full-replacement test stays 100." — names four factor quantities; counter_pct is a non-factor binding but baseline.rule is silent on it.
3. hazard_ext_outside_replacement_reimbursement: "Where the card cap uplift raises the cap, the out-of-area reimbursement base is the lower of the uplifted cap and Crestline's own price for the same tire." (names card-uplift and own-price factor quantities); "Out-of-area points from the two schedules below are added only to a prorated out-of-area coverage percentage, the sum then being held between 0 and 100; an out-of-area coverage percentage of 100 stays 100."; "Any out-of-area service allowance is added to the out-of-area reimbursement before that reimbursement is rounded."
4. hazard_ext_store_replacement_authorization: "Authorization points from the three schedules below are added only to a prorated authorization coverage percentage, the sum then being held between 0 and 100; an authorization coverage percentage of 100 stays 100."
5. hazard_ext_outside_repair_reimbursement: "The repair labor allowance, the repair card uplift and the repair fleet uplift below are added to the out-of-area repair reimbursement, and only the sum is rounded half up to the cent."
6. hazard_ext_outside_tow_reimbursement: "Where the tow light-truck rate, the tow card uplift or the tow fleet uplift below applies, the tow allowance is instead tow_reimbursement_cap times the tow light-truck rate, plus the tow card uplift and the tow fleet uplift, rounded half up to the cent."
Rendering: each factor document states what its own tiers add/multiply and on what (its effect), the computation document states the base assembly (rounding point, 0..100 hold, floor at 0.00) without naming any factor.

## Rule vs compute
7. hazard_ext_outside_replacement_reimbursement, Out-of-area proration measure: rule "otherwise the warranted_miles less the miles driven, times 100, divided by warranted_miles, rounded down to a whole percent" — compute outside_miles_pct floors the miles difference at 0 (MX(0, warranted - miles)); the rule states no floor. With points added after, a negative miles percentage differs from 0 (e.g. -10 + 7 points -> held at 0 vs 7). Rendered as the rule states (no floor).

## Binding homes
8. hazard_ext_outside_replacement_reimbursement: binding last_rotation_date belongs to no factor, yet only the proration-measure factor (rotation age tiers) and the tire-care-points factor (latest rotation fewer than 6 months ago) read it; baseline.rule never uses it. Placed in the computation document's covers (gate requirement), no prose there.
9. hazard_ext_outside_repair_reimbursement: repair_part, last_tow_claim, last_tow_paid, last_dispatch_claim, last_dispatch_paid carry the breakdown-limit factor's method but are not in that factor's bindings (computation document must cover them); same in hazard_ext_outside_tow_reimbursement for last_dispatch_claim, last_dispatch_paid and the result's limit arithmetic.

## Docstring vs body
10. confirm_life_of_tread_cancellation_58ab2fcf: docstring "One call records the holder's cancellation request as confirmed" — the body creates a NEW request row with status confirmed; an existing request awaiting confirmation is not updated (stays awaiting confirmation). Rendered as the docstring states the effect at capability level (a confirmed cancellation request is recorded).

## Overwrites (scoped)
11. Every overwrite here retires a base clause wholesale while its replaced_by keeps the base rule for every other case ("every other replacement keeps the base rule", "every other out-of-area claim keeps the base out-of-area condition", etc.). The retired clauses are therefore still in force outside each extended policy's scope. Rendered in the base documents as "no longer in force" only for the scope each replaced_by names, still in force otherwise.
12. hazard_ext_lot_cancellation_refund overwrite #3 retires "Remaining roadside calls lapse with the certificate." while its replaced_by keeps "the calls themselves still lapse with the certificate" — the overwrite retires a sentence that is still in force (the lapse) and only adds a credit. Rendered in the base cancellation document as retired in part: for the Life-of-Tread scope the calls still lapse, with a credit stated under the Life-of-Tread terms.
13. hazard_ext_lot_cancellation_refund: the day-count factor's methods ("from the date it is counted from to expiration_date") read the clock-start factor's output (refund_count_from) — a factor tier reading another factor's output. Rendered as "the date the share is counted from" without naming the other rule.
14. hazard_ext_outside_repair_reimbursement, Repair breakdown limit: the rule speaks of "an out-of-area tow reimbursement whose service date is no more than reimbursement_claim_window_days days before the reimbursement date" / "a Crestline roadside service entry whose service date is within that window" without saying which one when several exist; compute takes the most recent by service date (LATEST) and tests only that one. Rendered with "the tow or dispatch considered is the most recent one by service date" (compute-grounded precision, flagged for confirmation).
